clue.text: Reveal what the bride's father must do

definitions.meaning: to let slip a secret, as a tell-tale sign does

definitions.text: what the bride's father must do
definitions.meaning: at a traditional wedding the father hands his daughter over to the groom

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a bride's father has to do at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A tell-tale sign betrays a secret, and at a church wedding the father formally presents his daughter to the groom.

clue.text: Escape punishment? Go away!

definitions.meaning: to avoid a penalty or be acquitted
a rude command to leave, as in remove yourself

explanation.surface: A culprit dodges justice and is told to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off lightly is escaping a penalty; as a command it tells someone to leave.

clue.text: Manservant has a dance

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's personal manservant

explanation.surface: A butler takes part in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-time round dance in triple time, a ballroom favourite.

clue.text: Loved causing trouble to a Labourite

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado
red is the colour of the Labour Party, standing for a left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone adored for making trouble for a Labour MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British left-wing party; RED often stands for a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Loved in the past tense means cherished or worshipped.

clue.text: Better I speak after serving out meal

indicators.note: after places I and the word for speak after the reworked meal
serving out a meal spreads it about, so its letters are dished up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A waiter promises to make a speech once dinner has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving out' looks like waiting at table but is the anagram signal; 'after' sets I plus the word for speak behind it. 'Better' is a verb, to improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to improve, and better as a verb means improve.

clue.text: Saw rival tie the knot

parts.note: to rival someone is to compete or vie with them
an idiom for getting married, to wed

explanation.surface: Someone watched a rival get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Saw in the past tense means looked at or watched.

clue.text: Shut up!

parts.note: not a rude demand for quiet but to lock someone up, put behind bars

explanation.surface: An impatient demand for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone up in the sense of confining them is to jail them.

clue.text: Freeing woodlark may burden an employee

indicators.note: freeing the bird lets its letters loose to settle into a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing a songbird might give a zoo keeper extra duties.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of tasks given to a staff member can be a heavy load.

clue.text: Succeeds in getting dear before spring

parts.note: female deer are does
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A hunter prospers after bagging deer before reaching the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue puns on 'dear' sounding like deer; female deer are DOES. WELL is a spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper or thrive is to achieve success.

clue.text: Debate occurs when the lecture's finished

definitions.meaning: to discuss a matter thoroughly
once the speaking is done, the talk is at an end

explanation.surface: Discussion breaks out once the lecturer has stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something at length is a debate; and once a lecture ends, the speaking is literally finished.

clue.text: Small pears unusually thin on the ground

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters of pears are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: A fruit grower laments that small pears are scarce this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' signals an anagram of the fruit; the small S stands first.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin on the ground is an idiom for scarce or scattered, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Adjusted well after being given a slot

definitions.meaning: settled comfortably into a new group or place
squeezed into a space in a schedule

explanation.surface: A newcomer settled happily once given a place in the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adapts to a group belongs there; an appointment squeezed into a diary has been accommodated in a gap.

clue.text: Bolster military captive taking sick

indicators.note: the captive takes in, that is holds inside, the word for sick

parts.note: POW is the abbreviation for prisoner of war
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A captured soldier falls ill, and someone props him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolster' looks like a verb meaning support but is the noun, a long cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolster is a long cushion for the bed, a type of head rest.

clue.text: Used to be found on a clock

definitions.meaning: not new, previously owned

definitions.text: to be found on a clock
definitions.meaning: the thin pointer that marks the seconds

explanation.surface: A riddle about an old timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are not new; and the fast-moving pointer on a clock face marks the seconds.

clue.text: No-one gets charged for public affray

definitions.meaning: admission costs nothing for anybody
a brawl in a public place

explanation.surface: After a street brawl, the police decide nobody will face charges.
explanation.definitionFit: When nobody pays the entry is open to everyone, and a brawl involving everybody is an open melee.

clue.text: Virtually of equal worth

definitions.meaning: practically, nearly
matching in value

explanation.surface: Something that is practically as valuable as the original.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means practically or nearly, and also equally valuable in comparisons.

clue.text: It's played for the HQ dance

parts.note: headquarters, a military base
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: The band performs for a dance at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat-and-ball game, America's national pastime, is a sport one plays.

clue.text: Still indebted after setting up a trust

indicators.note: after places the word for indebted behind the word for still

parts.note: to still something is to stop or end it
indebted means owing money

explanation.surface: Someone still in debt after founding a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is a verb, to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a permanent fund to an institution, as when founding a trust.

clue.text: Little activity in a country of speculators

parts.note: a stag is a stock-market speculator who buys new shares to sell quickly
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A gloomy report on a country whose citizens all gamble on shares.
explanation.walkthrough: A STAG on the London stock exchange buys newly issued shares hoping to sell at once for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic stillness or lack of growth is a state of inactivity.

clue.text: Agency neither good nor bad

definitions.meaning: a means by which something is done
middling, average

explanation.surface: A verdict that an agency is merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: A means of communication or channel is an agency; and middling quality is between good and bad.

clue.text: Note article containing the fewest things possible

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A music writer's article includes as few notes as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: MINIM is the British name for a half note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the mathematical term for smallest values or least amounts.

clue.text: Packed as a precaution

definitions.meaning: placed inside a box or cover
to be prepared should something happen

explanation.surface: Someone packs an umbrella just to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Items boxed up are enclosed in a container; and the phrase also means as a safeguard.

clue.text: Old goner rehabilitated in America

indicators.note: rehabilitated means restored and reworked, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A has-been is given a fresh start across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rehabilitated' signals the anagram of the doomed person; 'in America' points to a US state rather than defining a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state on the Pacific coast, so a place found within the United States.

clue.text: She and I made admission of love and allegiance

indicators.note: admission is letting in, so the letter for love is admitted inside the anagram
made in the sense of formed, so the letters of she, and, I are formed into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Two people confess their love and declare their loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals the anagram of the three pronoun-and-link words; 'admission of' lets the tennis zero in just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm attachment or loyal support to a cause is a synonym for allegiance.

clue.text: Contract to acquire unfinished sketch

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a sketch is a drawing

explanation.surface: An artist signs a deal to buy an incomplete picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull inward or shrink, as a snail's horns do, is to contract.

clue.text: Graduate takes quartz from assembly-room

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
quartz is a form of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A geology graduate pockets crystals from a meeting hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the original Roman sense: a large public hall for meetings and law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the building was a large hall for public meetings and legal business.

clue.text: Wise man goes round Illinois for fodder

indicators.note: the wise man goes round, encircling, the state abbreviation

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois

explanation.surface: A sage travels through Illinois looking for animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass stored in a silo and fermented is winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Water privatisation could involve it!

definitions.meaning: a jocular term for plain drinking water
selling off a public water supply would be a sale of the first man's drink

explanation.surface: A dig at the selling off of the water companies.
explanation.walkthrough: Water was privatised in England and Wales in 1989; the phrase splits as a sale belonging to Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous old phrase for drinking water, the only drink of the first man in Eden.
